SM Moonir with Lokman Karim, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner.
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, Advocate ------ For the Respondent.
parties:
Mohammad Ali ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Bank and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Quddus J: This Rule Nisi at the instance of a judgment debtor in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question two orders dated 16-10-2008 and 4-11-2008 respectively passed by the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 75 of 2005 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 424 of 2004). By the first order the learned Judge, on an application tiled by the decree holder-bank, fixed a date of auction on publishing auction notice in newspapers for sale of the petitioner's mortgaged property, while by latter rejected his (petitioner's) application for rejection of the execution case. 

 2. Petitioners case is that Agrani Bank, Reazuddin Bazar Branch, Chittagong as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 424 of 2004 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong against the petitioner and two others for realisation of loan amounting to Taka 53,52,404.28 (Taka fifty-three lac fifty-two thousand four hundred four and Paisa twenty eight) only as calculated on 31-8-2004. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 18-2-2004 without sale of goods which were pledged by the petitioner as a primary security against his credit. The decree holder-bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 75 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong for execution of the decree, and filed an application seeking permission to sell the pledged goods and adjust the sale proceeds against the decretal amount. The executing Court allowed the application by order dated 20-4-2005 directing the bank to sell the goods and inform the Court within 31-5-2005. The bank failed to comply with the said order, even by making any attempt to that effect. Thereafter the bank filed another application for fixing a date of auction and publish notice in newspapers to sell the mortgaged property, which the Court allowed by order dated 16-10-2008. 

 3. The petitioner's further case is that he was not aware of the execution case till an auction notice was published in the Daily Amader Shomoy on 25-10-2008. Thereafter, on inquiry, he came to learn specifically about the execution case and filed an application for rejection of the case on the grounds: that the case was not disposed of within the statutory period prescribed in section 37 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the Ain); that the Artha Rin Suit was instituted without sale of pledged tea, which was under control of the bank as a primary security against credit facilities availed by the petitioner; that the decree was passed without any adjustment of pledge credit; that although the bank had obtained permission from the executing Court, the bank did not sell it or make any attempt to that effect. The learned Judge heard the said application and rejected it by order dated 4-11-2008. Challenging both the orders dated 16-10-2008 and 4-11-2008, the petitioner moved this Court, obtained the Rule and an order staying all further proceedings of the execution case. 

 4. The decree holder-bank as respondent No. 3 appears and contests the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the petitioner's allegation of obtaining the decree by the respondent-bank without adjustment of the pledge credit is a question of fact that can only be agitated in appeal, not in a writ petition. The bank also filed a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition stating that the petitioner availed cash credit (hypo) and credit (pledge) facilities from the respondent-bank pledging tea as a primary security and mortgaging some immovable properties as collateral. The bank on several occasions asked the petitioner to release the pledged goods on payment, but he did not pay heed, rather instituted Other Class Suit No. 81 of 2001 before the Senior Assistant Judge, First Court, Chittagong for perpetual injunction to restrain the bank from selling the pledged goods. Therefore the bank was constrained to file the present Artha Rin Suit for realisation of loan without selling the goods. In the said supplementary affidavit-in-opposition the bank admitted that although there was no ad-interim order of injunction against the bank in Other Class Suit No. 81 of 2001, it did not sell the goods under advise of its lawyer. The pledged goods were perishable and were already rotten, for which it could not be sold even in course of the execution proceedings. 

 6. Mr SM Moonir, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner supports the Rule and submits that the pledged goods were under control of the creditor-bank and in view of section 12(1)(2) of the Ain, sale of pledged goods is a precondition of filing an Artha Rin Suit. But the bank without so doing instituted the suit, obtained the decree and proceeded with the execution case and, as such, the suit, the decree in conclusion thereof and the execution case for execution of the said decree all are illegal and without lawful authority. He further submits that section 37 of the Ain provides 150 days time for concluding any execution case there under. The present execution case was filed on 26-2-2005 and has been continuing till today beyond the time prescribed in the special law and, as such, the proceeding in the execution case is without lawful authority. 

 7. On the other hand Mr Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-bank opposes the Rule and submits that as the petitioner instituted Other Class Suit No. 81 of 2001 for perpetual injunction to restrain the bank from selling the pledged tea, it could not sell the tea and was constrained to bring the Artha Rin Suit. The decree holder-bank with a bonafide intention obtained permission for selling the pledged goods from the executing Court, but ultimately failed as the goods were already rotten. The petitioner did not prefer any appeal against the decree passed in the Artha Rin Suit and the present writ petition challenging indirectly that the said decree is not maintainable, he submits. 

 11. In view of the above, the Rule is made absolute in part. The order dated 16-10-2008 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong Artha Rin Execution Case No. 75 of 2005 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 424 of 2004) fixing the date of auction and publishing the auction notices for sale of the mortgaged property is set-aside. The order of stay passed at the time of issuance of the Rule is vacated. The respondent-bank is directed to adjust the face value of the pledged lea, which was under its control at the time of filing the Artha Rin Suit, and to furnish a certificate statement of account to that effect before the executing Court. The executing Court will give the parties reasonable opportunity to appear and make their submissions on such statement of account and pass necessary order to its satisfaction. After such adjustment, the execution Court will be at liberty to proceed for holding fresh auction to sell the mortgaged property, if the decree is not yet satisfied.
